DNS caching matters because it affects how quickly and accurately domain names are resolved across a network. Without proper caching, every request may need to go through the full DNS resolution process, which can slow down access. Caching can improve performance by storing and returning previously resolved names, reducing latency and load. However, caching can also introduce inaccuracies if stale data is used, leading to incorrect or outdated information being delivered to users.
